title: One Person's Trash Is Another Person's Treasure

source.name: VOA Learning English — One Person's Trash Is Another Person's Treasure
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: People around the world share many things in common. But we are also different from each other. Not only do we look, think, and act differently, but we also like different things. Even identical twins may look the same but are very different individuals.
When we say one person's trash is another person's treasure , we mean that something that one person may consider worthless could be highly prized or valued by someone else.
Let’s hear an example of how to use this expression:
A: I really don't understand the appeal of Jackson Pollock’s paintings. To me, they look like a team of monkeys painted them!"
B: I love Pollock’s paintings. I see something new every time I look at them.
A: Well, I guess it's true what they say, one person's trash is another person's treasure .
Another expression with a similar meaning is different strokes for different folks .
This also means that different things appeal to different people. But as a set expression, we do not say “different strokes for different people.” That just doesn't sound right.

For example, a perfect evening for my friend is to go out and dance all night long. For me, a perfect evening is to stay at home with a book and a cup of tea. Neither is a better way to spend the evening. So, we should not judge. Or in other words, different strokes for different folks .
It takes all kinds to make the world go round.
They all mean … whatever makes you happy!
And all of these expressions have the same general meaning: We are all different and unique .

questions.q: Which situation best fits “one person’s trash is another person’s treasure”?
options: Nam gave away a comic book he no longer wanted, and his cousin was delighted to receive it
Nam sold his old comic book for less money than he had paid when he bought it
Nam threw away a torn comic book because nobody he knew wanted to read it
Nam and his cousin both disliked the comic book and agreed it was boring
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: thứ mà người này cho là vô giá trị lại được người khác trân trọng. Chỉ tình huống đầu tiên có hai người đánh giá khác nhau.

questions.q: Why does Speaker A say the paintings look as if a team of monkeys painted them?
options: To say that the artist painted the pictures together with some animals
To praise the paintings because they are playful and full of fun
To show that A does not think the paintings are skilful or attractive
To explain how the paintings were sold at an auction
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: A “doesn’t understand the appeal” của tranh Pollock; so sánh với khỉ vẽ = chê tranh không có kĩ thuật/đẹp.

questions.q: What does the writer say about “different strokes for different folks”?
options: Its wording is fixed, so changing “folks” to “people” sounds wrong
It is newer than the expression about trash and treasure
It can be changed freely without altering how the expression sounds
It is used only when people are talking about paintings and art
questions.explain: Đoạn 8: đây là thành ngữ cố định; “different strokes for different people” “just doesn’t sound right”.

questions.q: What does the writer’s example of a perfect evening show?
options: Dancing is a healthier hobby than reading quietly at home
Staying at home is always the better choice for an evening
People enjoy different things and neither choice is better
Friends should always choose the same activities together
questions.explain: Đoạn 9: một người thích khiêu vũ, người kia thích ở nhà đọc sách; “Neither is a better way” → mỗi người một sở thích.

questions.q: If someone says “whatever floats your boat”, what are they saying?
options: I accept that you like what you like
I do not trust your opinion
I want to buy your boat
I think you should try something new
questions.explain: Đoạn 11–13: những thành ngữ này đều có nghĩa chấp nhận mỗi người mỗi sở thích (“whatever makes you happy”).

questions.q: In the example, Speaker B finds something new in the paintings every time B looks at them.
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: B “see something new every time I look at them”.

questions.q: Jackson Pollock was born in the United States.
questions.explain: Bài không nói gì về nơi sinh của Jackson Pollock.
